newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban punish women on dress code.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban punish women on dress code.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic movement punished 60 women on Sunday in the capital Kabul for violating its strict Islamic dress code, Kabul's state radio reported.

The broadcast, monitored in Islamabad, said the women from various parts of Kabul were punished for flouting the strict orders of the Taleban government's commission on "promoting good and banning evil".

It did not specify the punishment, but in the past Taleban militiamen have beaten women with sticks for moving out of their homes without wearing a "burqa", a head-to-toe robe which conceals the face with a cloth mesh.

The radio said commission teams also visited a military hospital and government offices in Kabul on Sunday to see if the staff observed the Islamic Sharia code, which also requires men to grow long beards and wear the traditional turban or cap.

The Taleban, which captured Kabul in September last year from forces loyal to ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and now control more than two thirds of Afghanistan, has vowed to implement strict Islamic Sharia law throughout the country.
